name: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab
bio: A leading companion of the Prophet, peace be upon him, whose acceptance of Islam strengthened the early Muslim community. As caliph from 634 to 644 he presided over rapid expansion and built many of the institutions of the early Islamic state, becoming a byword for justice and personal accountability.
achievements: Established the diwan (state registry) and public treasury administration
Adopted the Hijri calendar
Known as al-Faruq, the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood
works: Sayings and rulings preserved in the hadith collections and early histories

name: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib
role: Fourth caliph; cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet
bio: Raised in the Prophet's household and among the first to accept Islam, 'Ali was renowned for his knowledge, eloquence and courage. He served as the fourth caliph from 656 to 661. Many sayings of wisdom are attributed to him, though scholars caution that some attributions are weak.
achievements: One of the earliest Muslims
Celebrated for eloquence and judicial wisdom
Fourth of the rightly guided caliphs
works: Sayings preserved in hadith and adab literature

name: 'A'ishah bint Abi Bakr
role: Mother of the Believers; scholar and narrator
bio: Wife of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and daughter of Abu Bakr. After his death she became one of the most important teachers in Madinah, consulted by senior companions on law, medicine, poetry and the Prophet's private practice.
achievements: Among the most prolific narrators of hadith, with over two thousand reports
Taught many of the leading scholars of the next generation
Key source on the Prophet's household life
works: Her narrations throughout Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim

name: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas
bio: A cousin of the Prophet, peace be upon him, who prayed that Allah grant him understanding of the religion and knowledge of interpretation. Ibn 'Abbas became the foremost early authority on tafsir, and his explanations are cited throughout later commentaries such as those of al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir.
achievements: Founder of the Makkan school of tafsir
Teacher of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and other leading successors
Known as Tarjuman al-Qur'an and Hibr al-Ummah
works: Interpretations transmitted in al-Tabari's and Ibn Kathir's tafsir

name: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf
bio: One of the earliest Muslims and among the ten companions given glad tidings of Paradise. Arriving in Madinah with nothing, he declined a share of his host's wealth and asked to be shown the market, building a large trading fortune that he spent generously in the way of Allah.
achievements: One of the ten promised Paradise
Model of honest, generous trade
Member of the consultative council that chose 'Uthman
works: Reports in Jami' al-Tirmidhi and the sirah literature

name: Khalid ibn al-Walid
bio: A brilliant commander who fought against the Muslims at Uhud before accepting Islam. He went on to lead decisive campaigns in Arabia, Iraq and Syria, including Yarmuk, and was given the title Sayf Allah, the Sword of Allah. He died in his bed in Homs.
achievements: Commanded at Mu'tah and Yarmuk
Titled Sayf Allah by the Prophet
Studied in military history for tactical skill
works: Accounts in the early histories of al-Tabari and others

name: Hasan al-Basri
bio: Born in Madinah and raised among the companions, Hasan al-Basri became the most famous preacher of Basra. His sermons on accountability, the shortness of life and sincerity shaped generations of scholars and ascetics.
achievements: Leading figure of the generation after the companions
Renowned for powerful sermons on time and accountability
Teacher of many early scholars
works: Sayings preserved in early biographical and zuhd works

name: Mujahid ibn Jabr
bio: The leading student of Ibn 'Abbas in tafsir, Mujahid is reported to have reviewed the whole Qur'an with his teacher several times, asking about each verse. His interpretations are a foundation of classical tafsir.
achievements: Principal student of Ibn 'Abbas
Major source in al-Tabari's and Ibn Kathir's tafsir

name: Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad
bio: According to the biographers, al-Fudayl was a highway robber whose life changed when he heard a verse of the Qur'an recited at night. He became one of the most respected ascetics and teachers of Makkah.
achievements: Celebrated example of sincere repentance
Teacher of Ibn al-Mubarak and others
works: Sayings recorded by al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala'

name: Ibn Ishaq
bio: Muhammad ibn Ishaq compiled one of the earliest comprehensive biographies of the Prophet, peace be upon him. His work survives mainly through the later edition of Ibn Hisham and remains a primary source for the sirah.
achievements: Author of the earliest major sirah
Source for later historians including al-Tabari
works: Sirat Rasul Allah (via Ibn Hisham's edition)

name: Imam al-Bukhari
bio: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari travelled widely to collect hadith and applied strict conditions to their chains of narration. His Sahih is regarded by Sunni scholars as the most authentic book after the Qur'an.
achievements: Compiled Sahih al-Bukhari over about sixteen years
Set exacting standards for authenticating narrators
Wrote major works on narrator criticism

name: Imam Muslim
bio: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, a student of al-Bukhari, compiled the second most respected hadith collection in Sunni Islam, known for its careful arrangement of different chains of the same report side by side.
achievements: Compiled Sahih Muslim
Renowned for precise arrangement of narrations

name: Imam al-Tirmidhi
bio: A student of al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi compiled one of the six canonical hadith collections. He was among the first to grade each hadith and to record the legal opinions of different schools alongside it.
achievements: Compiled Jami' al-Tirmidhi, one of the six canonical books
Pioneered systematic grading of hadith

name: Imam Abu Dawud
bio: Abu Dawud Sulayman al-Sijistani compiled a collection focused on hadith used in law. It became one of the six canonical books and a primary reference for jurists.
achievements: Compiled Sunan Abi Dawud
Student of Ahmad ibn Hanbal

name: Imam Ibn Majah
bio: Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah compiled the Sunan that most scholars count as the sixth of the canonical hadith books.
achievements: Compiled Sunan Ibn Majah

name: Imam al-Nawawi
bio: Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi lived only about forty-five years, yet his books are among the most widely read in the Muslim world. He combined deep scholarship with an ascetic life and outspoken integrity before rulers.
achievements: Author of Riyad al-Salihin and the Forty Hadith
Leading authority of the Shafi'i school
Wrote a celebrated commentary on Sahih Muslim

name: Imam al-Shafi'i
role: Founder of the Shafi'i school of law
bio: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i studied with Imam Malik and later in Iraq, then settled in Egypt. His Risala is regarded as the first systematic work on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence. He was also a celebrated poet.
achievements: Founded the Shafi'i school of law
Wrote the first systematic work of usul al-fiqh
Famous verses on knowledge, patience and friendship

name: Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
role: Hadith master; founder of the Hanbali school
bio: Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled one of the largest hadith collections and became the eponym of the Hanbali school. His steadfastness during the mihna, the state-imposed inquisition, made him a model of principled patience.
achievements: Compiled the Musnad
Endured imprisonment for his convictions
Teacher of Abu Dawud and many others

name: Al-Tabari
bio: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari wrote the most important early commentary on the Qur'an, gathering the interpretations of the companions and their successors with their chains. His universal history is equally foundational.
achievements: Author of the foundational tafsir Jami' al-Bayan
Author of a monumental history of prophets and kings

name: Ibn Hazm
bio: Born in Córdoba to a family of officials, Ibn Hazm served in politics before devoting himself to scholarship. He wrote on law, theology, comparative religion, love and ethics, and was the leading representative of the Zahiri school.
achievements: Leading figure of the Zahiri school
Pioneer of comparative religion
Wrote a classic on the psychology of love
works: Al-Akhlaq wa al-Siyar fi Mudawat al-Nufus
Tawq al-Hamamah (The Ring of the Dove)

name: Imam al-Ghazali
role: Theologian, jurist and reviver of religious sciences
bio: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali was the leading professor at the Nizamiyya in Baghdad when a spiritual crisis led him to leave his post and seek certainty. The result was the Ihya, a vast work uniting law, ethics and the inner life. He is known as Hujjat al-Islam, the Proof of Islam.
achievements: Wrote the Ihya 'Ulum al-Din
Titled Hujjat al-Islam
Shaped Islamic ethics, theology and spirituality for centuries
works: Ihya 'Ulum al-Din (Revival of the Religious Sciences)

name: Ibn Taymiyyah
bio: Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah fled the Mongol advance as a child and grew into one of the most influential and prolific scholars of Islamic history. He wrote on theology, law, governance and spirituality, and died imprisoned in the citadel of Damascus.
achievements: Prolific writer across theology, law and politics
Teacher of Ibn al-Qayyim, Ibn Kathir and al-Dhahabi
Wrote a key work on governance by the Shari'ah

name: Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
role: Scholar of the heart, law and ethics
bio: The closest student of Ibn Taymiyyah, imprisoned with him for a time, Ibn al-Qayyim wrote with unusual warmth and psychological depth about patience, love of Allah, repentance and the diseases of the heart.
achievements: Wrote classic works on the spiritual stations
Combined law, hadith and psychology of the soul
Edited and spread his teacher's thought

name: Al-Dhahabi
bio: Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi was a master of narrator biography and history. His Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' remains a standard reference on the lives of scholars.
achievements: Author of major biographical dictionaries
Leading critic of hadith narrators

name: Ibn Kathir
bio: Isma'il ibn Kathir studied with Ibn Taymiyyah and al-Mizzi in Damascus. His tafsir explains the Qur'an through the Qur'an itself, the hadith and the sayings of the early generations, and is among the most widely read commentaries today.
achievements: Author of one of the most used tafsirs
Wrote a universal history from creation to his own time

name: Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali
bio: Ibn Rajab is best known for his commentary on al-Nawawi's Forty Hadith, which he expanded to fifty, explaining each with legal and spiritual depth.
achievements: Wrote the classic commentary on the Forty Hadith
Combined hadith scholarship with spiritual insight

name: Ibn Ata'illah al-Iskandari
bio: A scholar of Alexandria who became a master of the Shadhili spiritual path, Ibn Ata'illah is best known for the Hikam, a book of aphorisms on trust in Allah, sincerity and the inner life that has been taught for seven centuries.
achievements: Author of al-Hikam, one of the most commented works of Islamic spirituality
Third master of the Shadhili path

name: Ibn Jama'ah
bio: Badr al-Din ibn Jama'ah served as chief judge in Egypt and Syria and wrote a well-known manual on the ethics of teachers and students.
achievements: Chief judge in Cairo and Damascus
Wrote a classic of Islamic educational ethics

name: Ibn Khaldun
bio: Born in Tunis, Ibn Khaldun served at several North African courts before writing the Muqaddimah, an introduction to history that analysed society, economics and the rise and fall of states. He later served as a Maliki judge in Cairo.
achievements: Often called a founder of sociology and economic history
Developed the concept of 'asabiyyah
Served as Maliki chief judge in Cairo

name: Marcus Aurelius
bio: Emperor of Rome from 161 to 180, Marcus Aurelius spent much of his reign on military campaigns. His private notebook, written in Greek and never intended for publication, became one of the most read works of practical philosophy.
achievements: Ruled the Roman Empire for nearly two decades
Wrote Meditations, a classic of Stoic self-discipline

name: Seneca
bio: Lucius Annaeus Seneca, born in Córdoba, was a philosopher, playwright and adviser to the emperor Nero. His essays and letters on time, anger and adversity remain widely read.
achievements: Leading Roman Stoic writer
Influential essays on time and the good life

name: Aristotle
bio: Student of Plato and teacher of Alexander the Great, Aristotle wrote on logic, ethics, politics, rhetoric and science. His works were translated and studied intensively by Muslim philosophers, who called him 'the First Teacher'.
achievements: Founded formal logic
Shaped ethics and rhetoric for two millennia
Deeply studied in classical Islamic philosophy

name: Ronald Heifetz
bio: A physician and cellist by training, Heifetz co-founded the Center for Public Leadership at Harvard Kennedy School and developed the adaptive leadership framework, distinguishing technical problems from adaptive challenges.
achievements: Developed adaptive leadership
Founding director of Harvard's Center for Public Leadership
works: Leadership on the Line (with Marty Linsky)

name: Bill George
role: Former CEO of Medtronic; leadership professor
bio: Bill George led Medtronic as chief executive from 1991 to 2001, during which its market value grew dramatically, then joined Harvard Business School, where he researched and taught authentic leadership.
achievements: CEO of Medtronic 1991–2001
Developed the 'True North' approach to authentic leadership

name: Daniel Goleman
bio: A psychologist who reported on behavioural science for The New York Times, Goleman popularised emotional intelligence and its role in leadership, arguing it matters more than IQ for many kinds of success.
achievements: Popularised emotional intelligence worldwide
Wrote one of HBR's most requested articles, 'What Makes a Leader'

name: Amy Edmondson
bio: Edmondson's research on hospital teams led to the concept of team psychological safety. She was ranked the world's top management thinker by Thinkers50 in 2021.
achievements: Defined team psychological safety
Thinkers50 top management thinker, 2021

name: John Kotter
bio: A long-serving Harvard Business School professor, Kotter's eight-step model for leading change is among the most widely used frameworks for organisational transformation.
achievements: Created the eight-step process for leading change
Founded Kotter International

name: Frances Frei
role: Professor of technology and operations management
bio: Frei researches trust, service and leadership. She was brought in as Uber's senior vice president for leadership and strategy in 2017 to help repair its culture, and co-wrote several books with Anne Morriss.
achievements: Developed the trust triangle: authenticity, logic and empathy
Advised organisations through culture crises
works: Move Fast and Fix Things (with Anne Morriss)

name: Daniel Kahneman
bio: With Amos Tversky, Kahneman showed how human judgement departs systematically from rational models, founding behavioural economics. He received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2002.
achievements: Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, 2002
Co-created prospect theory with Amos Tversky
Popularised System 1 and System 2 thinking

name: Philip Tetlock
bio: Tetlock's long-term study of expert predictions showed that most experts forecast poorly, but that some people, 'superforecasters', are consistently accurate. He co-founded the Good Judgment Project.
achievements: Ran a twenty-year study of expert forecasts
Co-led the Good Judgment Project's tournament wins

name: Charlie Munger
role: Investor; vice chairman of Berkshire Hathaway
bio: Warren Buffett's long-time partner, Munger was famous for his 'latticework of mental models' and his talks on human misjudgement, which drew on many disciplines.
achievements: Vice chairman of Berkshire Hathaway
Influential advocate of multidisciplinary thinking

name: Annie Duke
role: Former professional poker player; decision strategist
bio: Duke studied cognitive psychology at graduate level, then became a champion poker player before writing on decision-making under uncertainty.
achievements: World Series of Poker bracelet winner
Popularised the concept of 'resulting'

name: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
role: Essayist, former trader and risk scholar
bio: A former options trader, Taleb writes on uncertainty, probability and risk in his multi-volume Incerto, introducing the ideas of Black Swans and antifragility.
achievements: Popularised the 'Black Swan' concept
Developed the idea of antifragility

name: Michael Porter
bio: Porter's five forces framework and his definition of strategy as unique positioning with trade-offs are taught in business schools worldwide. He is a University Professor at Harvard.
achievements: Created the five forces framework
Defined the value chain
Among the most cited scholars in management

name: W. Chan Kim & Renée Mauborgne
bio: Kim and Mauborgne co-direct the INSEAD Blue Ocean Strategy Institute. Their research on value innovation argues that companies thrive by creating uncontested market space.
achievements: Developed blue ocean strategy
Created the ERRC grid and strategy canvas

name: Clayton Christensen
bio: Christensen developed the theory of disruptive innovation and the 'jobs to be done' framework. A man of deep faith, he also wrote on how to measure a life well lived.
achievements: Developed disruptive innovation theory
Created the jobs-to-be-done framework
works: How Will You Measure Your Life?

name: Richard Rumelt
bio: Rumelt is known for distinguishing good strategy, a coherent response to a diagnosed challenge, from bad strategy built on fluff and goals.
achievements: Defined the 'kernel' of good strategy

name: Robert Kaplan & David Norton
bio: Kaplan, a Harvard Business School professor, and consultant David Norton introduced the balanced scorecard in 1992, linking financial, customer, process and learning measures to strategy.
achievements: Created the balanced scorecard
Developed strategy maps

name: Roger Fisher & William Ury
bio: Fisher and Ury founded the Harvard Negotiation Project in 1979. Their method of principled negotiation has been used in business, diplomacy and peace processes.
achievements: Founded the Harvard Negotiation Project
Introduced BATNA and interest-based negotiation
works: The Power of a Positive No (Ury)

name: Douglas Stone & Sheila Heen
bio: Stone and Heen taught negotiation at Harvard Law School and co-founded Triad Consulting. Their books address the hardest conversations at work and home.
achievements: Developed the 'three conversations' framework
Analysed the triggers that block feedback

name: Robert Cialdini
bio: Cialdini spent years studying professional persuaders, including undercover in sales training, and identified the core principles that lead people to say yes.
achievements: Identified the principles of influence
Influence is among the best-known psychology books

name: Adam Grant
bio: Grant became the youngest tenured professor at Wharton. He researches motivation, generosity and rethinking, and writes widely read books on work and life.
achievements: Research on givers, takers and matchers
Popular TED speaker and author

name: Robert Putnam
bio: Putnam's work on social capital showed how networks of trust and civic association shape the health of democracies and economies.
achievements: Popularised the concept of social capital
National Humanities Medal, 2012

name: Mark Granovetter
bio: Granovetter's 1973 paper on the strength of weak ties is one of the most cited in social science, showing how acquaintances bring new information and opportunities.
achievements: Wrote 'The Strength of Weak Ties'

name: Robert Waldinger
role: Psychiatrist; director of the Harvard Study of Adult Development
bio: Waldinger directs one of the longest studies of human life, begun in 1938. His TED talk on what makes a good life is among the most watched ever.
achievements: Director of the Harvard Study of Adult Development

name: Peter Drucker
bio: Often called the father of modern management, Drucker wrote nearly forty books on management, society and the knowledge worker. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2002.
achievements: Defined modern management as a discipline
Coined the term 'knowledge worker'

name: Robert Kegan & Lisa Lahey
bio: Kegan and Lahey study how adults grow in mental complexity, and developed the 'immunity to change' method for uncovering hidden competing commitments.
achievements: Developed the immunity to change map
Theory of adult mental development (Kegan)

name: Arthur C. Brooks
bio: A former professional musician and president of the American Enterprise Institute (2009–2019), Brooks teaches a popular course on happiness at Harvard and writes about meaning and ageing well.
achievements: Teaches leadership and happiness at Harvard
Writes the 'How to Build a Life' column
works: Build the Life You Want (with Oprah Winfrey)

name: James Clear
bio: Clear's writing on habits and continuous improvement became Atomic Habits, which has sold tens of millions of copies worldwide.
achievements: Author of one of the best-selling habit books of all time

name: Cal Newport
bio: A professor of computer science, Newport writes about focus, technology and meaningful work, arguing that deep concentration is an increasingly rare and valuable skill.
achievements: Popularised 'deep work' and digital minimalism
works: So Good They Can't Ignore You

name: Greg McKeown
bio: McKeown advises organisations on focus and wrote Essentialism, a guide to the disciplined pursuit of less but better.
achievements: Popularised essentialism

name: Stephen R. Covey
bio: Covey's book on seven habits of effective people, grounded in character and principles, became one of the best-selling business books ever.
achievements: Wrote The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
Co-founded FranklinCovey
works: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People

name: Charles Duhigg
bio: A Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter for The New York Times, Duhigg writes about the science of habits, productivity and communication.
achievements: Shared the 2013 Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting

name: Oliver Burkeman
bio: Long-time Guardian columnist on psychology, Burkeman writes on time, mortality and the limits of productivity.
achievements: Popular writer on time and limits

name: Carol Dweck
bio: Dweck's research on implicit theories of ability led to the fixed and growth mindset framework, used in schools and organisations worldwide. She won the Yidan Prize for Education Research in 2017.
achievements: Developed mindset theory
Yidan Prize for Education Research, 2017

name: Viktor Frankl
bio: A Viennese psychiatrist who survived Nazi concentration camps including Auschwitz, Frankl founded logotherapy, a therapy centred on the human search for meaning.
achievements: Founded logotherapy
Survived the Holocaust camps

name: Angela Duckworth
bio: Duckworth studies grit and self-control, and co-founded Character Lab. She was named a MacArthur Fellow in 2013.
achievements: MacArthur Fellow, 2013
Developed the grit scale

name: David Epstein
bio: A former Sports Illustrated writer, Epstein investigates talent, expertise and learning, arguing for the value of breadth in a specialised world.
achievements: Author of two bestsellers on talent and learning

name: Morgan Housel
bio: A partner at the Collaborative Fund and former columnist, Housel writes about the psychology behind financial decisions.
achievements: The Psychology of Money became a global bestseller

name: George S. Clason
bio: Clason wrote a series of pamphlets of financial parables set in ancient Babylon, later collected into a book that remains popular a century on.
achievements: Author of a long-lasting personal finance classic

name: Thomas J. Stanley & William D. Danko
bio: Stanley and Danko surveyed wealthy Americans and found most lived modestly and accumulated wealth through frugality, self-employment and disciplined investing.
achievements: Influential research on how millionaires actually live

name: Vicki Robin & Joe Dominguez
bio: Robin and Dominguez developed a programme for transforming one's relationship with money, treating it as life energy.
achievements: Pioneers of the financial independence movement

name: Dale Carnegie
role: Teacher of public speaking and human relations
bio: Carnegie's courses and books on public speaking and dealing with people became a worldwide training movement that continues today.
achievements: Founded Dale Carnegie Training
One of the best-selling self-help books of all time
works: How to Win Friends and Influence People
How to Stop Worrying and Start Living

name: Chris Voss
bio: Voss served as the FBI's lead international kidnapping negotiator before founding the Black Swan Group, teaching negotiation to businesses.
achievements: Lead international kidnapping negotiator for the FBI
works: Never Split the Difference (with Tahl Raz)

name: Simon Sinek
bio: Sinek's 2009 talk on the 'golden circle' became one of the most watched TED talks, and led to a series of books on purpose and leadership.
achievements: Popularised 'start with why'

name: Kerry Patterson, Joseph Grenny, Ron McMillan & Al Switzler
bio: Co-founders of VitalSmarts, now Crucial Learning, this group researched how people handle high-stakes conversations and accountability at work.
achievements: Developed the Crucial Conversations training used worldwide

name: Jim Collins
bio: Collins studies what distinguishes great companies from good ones, introducing the idea of Level 5 leadership: personal humility combined with professional will.
achievements: Defined Level 5 leadership

name: John Gottman
bio: Gottman studied thousands of couples over decades, identifying behaviours that predict whether relationships last. He co-founded the Gottman Institute with his wife, Julie Schwartz Gottman.
achievements: Identified predictors of lasting relationships
Co-founded the Gottman Institute
works: The Seven Principles for Making Marriage Work (with Nan Silver)

name: Jonathan Haidt
bio: Haidt researches moral psychology and, more recently, the effects of smartphones and social media on young people's mental health.
achievements: Influential research on moral psychology and youth mental health

name: Shehu Usman dan Fodio
role: Scholar, reformer and founder of the Sokoto Caliphate
bio: A Fulani scholar who taught and preached reform across Hausaland, Usman dan Fodio led a movement from 1804 that established the Sokoto Caliphate, one of the largest states in nineteenth-century Africa. He wrote extensively in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa.
achievements: Founded the Sokoto Caliphate
Wrote over a hundred works on law, theology and governance
Championed education, including of women

name: Nana Asma'u
bio: Daughter of Usman dan Fodio, Nana Asma'u was fluent in Arabic, Fulfulde, Hausa and Tamasheq. She wrote poetry on history, law and devotion, and built the Yan Taru network of women teachers who spread education across the caliphate.
achievements: Founded the Yan Taru women's education network
Wrote dozens of poems in four languages
A model of Muslim women's scholarship in West Africa
works: Collected poetry and prose (Collected Works of Nana Asma'u, ed. Boyd and Mack)

name: Chinua Achebe
bio: Achebe's first novel, Things Fall Apart, became the most widely read African novel and transformed how Africa was written about. He also wrote sharply on Nigerian leadership and politics.
achievements: Wrote Things Fall Apart, translated into over fifty languages
Man Booker International Prize, 2007
Often called the father of modern African literature

name: Wole Soyinka
bio: Soyinka became the first African to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986. He was imprisoned during the Nigerian Civil War and has long campaigned against tyranny.
achievements: Nobel Prize in Literature, 1986
Lifelong advocate for freedom and justice

name: Nelson Mandela
role: Anti-apartheid leader; President of South Africa
bio: Imprisoned for twenty-seven years for opposing apartheid, Mandela emerged to lead negotiations for a democratic South Africa and served as its first democratically elected president from 1994 to 1999.
achievements: Nobel Peace Prize, 1993
First democratically elected President of South Africa
Symbol of reconciliation

name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
bio: Okonjo-Iweala twice served as Nigeria's finance minister and was a managing director of the World Bank. In 2021 she became the first woman and first African to lead the World Trade Organization.
achievements: Nigeria's finance minister (2003–06, 2011–15)
First woman and first African Director-General of the WTO, 2021

name: Dora Akunyili
bio: As Director-General of NAFDAC from 2001 to 2008, Akunyili led a determined campaign against counterfeit drugs and survived an assassination attempt in 2003. She later served as Minister of Information.
achievements: Led Nigeria's fight against fake drugs
Received numerous national and international integrity awards

name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
bio: Adichie's novels about Nigeria and its diaspora have won major prizes, and her 2009 talk 'The Danger of a Single Story' is among the most watched TED talks.
achievements: Orange Prize for Fiction, 2007
MacArthur Fellow, 2008

name: Taiichi Ohno
role: Industrial engineer, architect of the Toyota Production System
bio: Ohno joined Toyota in 1943 and spent decades on the factory floor developing the system of just-in-time production, built-in quality and continuous improvement that became known as lean manufacturing. He rose to executive vice-president of Toyota Motor Corporation.
achievements: Developed the Toyota Production System
Popularised the five whys and the seven wastes
Influenced manufacturing and service industries worldwide
works: Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production

name: Kazuo Inamori
bio: An engineer from Kagoshima, Inamori founded Kyocera in 1959 and DDI, later KDDI, in 1984. In 2010, aged 78, he became unpaid chairman of the bankrupt Japan Airlines and led its turnaround. He wrote widely on ethics in business and life.
achievements: Founded Kyocera and KDDI
Led the turnaround of Japan Airlines, relisted in 2012
Created amoeba management
Established the Kyoto Prize

name: Miyamoto Musashi
bio: Japan's most celebrated swordsman, said to have been undefeated in some sixty duels, Musashi spent his final years in Kumamoto, where he wrote The Book of Five Rings in a cave known as Reigandō. He was also an accomplished painter and calligrapher.
achievements: Founded the Niten Ichi-ryū school of swordsmanship
Wrote a classic of strategy still read worldwide
works: The Book of Five Rings (Go Rin no Sho)

name: Sun Tzu
bio: Traditionally identified as a general serving the state of Wu in ancient China, Sun Tzu is credited with The Art of War. Historians debate the details of his life and the text's exact date, but the book has been studied by generals, statesmen and business leaders for over two thousand years.
achievements: Author of the oldest surviving treatise on strategy
Influenced military and business thought worldwide

name: Confucius
bio: Kong Fuzi, known in the West as Confucius, was a teacher and minor official who travelled among the states of ancient China urging rulers to govern by virtue. His sayings, collected by his disciples in the Analects, shaped the education, ethics and government of China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam.
achievements: Founded the Confucian tradition of ethics and learning
Shaped East Asian education and civil service for two millennia

name: Lee Kuan Yew
bio: Lee led Singapore as prime minister from 1959 to 1990, through independence in 1965 and rapid transformation into a wealthy trading and financial hub known for clean government. His record also drew criticism for restrictions on political opposition and the press.
achievements: Prime Minister of Singapore, 1959–1990
Led Singapore's development from developing to high-income nation
Built a reputation for low corruption and meritocracy

name: Ibn al-Haytham
bio: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham, known in Latin Europe as Alhazen, was born in Basra and worked in Cairo. His Book of Optics combined mathematics with careful experiment, explained vision as light entering the eye and profoundly influenced European science after its Latin translation.
achievements: Wrote the seven-volume Book of Optics
Pioneered systematic experiment in physics
Studied the camera obscura and the nature of light

name: Malek Bennabi
bio: Trained as an electrical engineer in Paris, Bennabi devoted his life to analysing why the Muslim world declined and how it could recover. His books on the problems of civilisation influenced generations of Muslim thinkers in North Africa and beyond.
achievements: Developed the concept of 'colonisability'
Wrote the series Problems of Civilisation
works: The Problem of Ideas in the Muslim World

name: Kautilya (Chanakya)
bio: Tradition identifies Kautilya, also called Chanakya, as the adviser who helped Chandragupta Maurya found the Maurya Empire. The Arthashastra attributed to him is a detailed treatise on statecraft, economics and administration; scholars believe the text was compiled and revised over several centuries.
achievements: Attributed author of the Arthashastra
Remembered as a master of statecraft in Indian tradition

name: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
role: Aerospace scientist and 11th President of India
bio: The son of a boat owner and local imam in Rameswaram, Kalam studied aeronautical engineering and led India's first satellite launch vehicle and its missile programme. He served as President of India from 2002 to 2007 and devoted his later life to inspiring students.
achievements: Project director of SLV-3, which launched India's Rohini satellite in 1980
Led India's integrated guided missile programme
President of India, 2002–2007
Bharat Ratna, 1997

name: Amartya Sen
bio: Sen grew up in Bengal and witnessed the 1943 famine as a child. His work on famines, welfare economics and human capabilities earned him the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 and helped shape the UN's Human Development Index.
achievements: Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, 1998
Developed the capability approach
Influenced the Human Development Index

name: Sejong the Great
role: Fourth king of the Joseon dynasty
bio: King Sejong reigned from 1418 to 1450 and is regarded as one of Korea's greatest rulers. He oversaw the creation of the Korean alphabet, supported scholarship and science, reformed taxation through wide consultation and introduced humane measures for the poor.
achievements: Promulgated the Korean alphabet, Hangul, in 1446
Sponsored advances in astronomy, timekeeping and agriculture
Conducted a nationwide consultation on tax reform in 1430

name: Said Nursi
bio: Known as Bediuzzaman, 'the wonder of the age', Nursi was a Kurdish-born Islamic scholar in the late Ottoman Empire and early Turkish Republic. Exiled and imprisoned for many years, he wrote the Risale-i Nur, a vast commentary on Qur'anic teachings that his students copied by hand and spread widely.
achievements: Wrote the Risale-i Nur collection
Delivered the Damascus Sermon in 1911
Inspired a major faith-renewal movement in Turkey

name: Ahi Evran
role: Scholar and craftsman, patron of the Ahi guilds
bio: Shaykh Nasir al-Din Mahmud, remembered as Ahi Evran, was a scholar and leather tanner in Seljuk Anatolia. Turkish tradition honours him as the founder or patron of the Ahi brotherhoods, which combined craft training, business ethics, faith and hospitality.
achievements: Revered patron of the Anatolian Ahi craft guilds
Symbol of ethical trade and craftsmanship in Turkish culture
works: Treatises on ethics and philosophy attributed to him

name: Muhammad Iqbal
bio: Born in Sialkot in British India, Iqbal studied at Cambridge and earned a doctorate in Munich. His Urdu and Persian poetry, and his lectures on Islamic thought, called Muslims to self-renewal and active faith. He is regarded as the spiritual father of Pakistan.
achievements: Major poet in Urdu and Persian
Delivered the lectures on the reconstruction of Islamic thought
Proposed a Muslim homeland in his 1930 Allahabad address
works: The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam

name: Syed Muhammad Naquib al-Attas
bio: Born in Java and raised in Malaysia, al-Attas studied at McGill and the University of London. He founded the International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilization in Kuala Lumpur and wrote influential works on the Islamic vision of knowledge, education and the human being.
achievements: Founded ISTAC in Kuala Lumpur
Developed the concept of ta'dib in Islamic education
Major scholar of Malay Islamic history
works: The Concept of Education in Islam
Prolegomena to the Metaphysics of Islam
